arxiv-2110-05734.creator: Chao Yu, Xinyi Yang, Jiaxuan Gao, Huazhong Yang, Yu Wang, Yi Wu, [0.5ex] Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences, Tsinghua University, [0.5ex] Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute, [0.5ex] zoeyuchao@gmail.com, jxwuyi@gmail.com
arxiv-2110-05734.description: Abstract We tackle the problem of cooperative visual exploration where multiple agents need to jointly explore unseen regions as fast as possible based on visual signals. Classical planning-based methods often suffer from expensive computation overhead at each step and a limited expressiveness of complex cooperation strategy.

arxiv-2204-10251.title: Layered Complex Networks as Fluctuation Amplifiers
arxiv-2204-10251.creator: Melvyn Tyloo
arxiv-2204-10251.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Melvyn Tyloo. In complex networked systems theory, an important question is how to evaluate the system robustness to external perturbations. With this task in mind, I investigate the propagation of noise in multi-layer networked systems. I find that, for a two layer network, noise originally injected in one layer can be strongly amplified in the other layer, depending on how well-connected are the complex networks in each layer and on how much the eigenmodes of their Laplacian matrices overlap.

arxiv-2210-16074.title: Improving Chest X-Ray Classification by RNN-based Patient Monitoring
arxiv-2210-16074.creator: 1 st David Biesner, 2 nd Helen Schneider, 3 rd Benjamin Wulff, 4 th Ulrike Attenberger, 5 th Rafet Sifa
arxiv-2210-16074.description: Abstract Chest X-Ray imaging is one of the most common radiological tools for detection of various pathologies related to the chest area and lung function. In a clinical setting, automated assessment of chest radiographs has the potential of assisting physicians in their decision making process and optimize clinical workflows, for example by prioritizing emergency patients.

arxiv-2303-16273.title: Vacuum birefringence and dichroism in a strong plane-wave background
arxiv-2303-16273.creator: I. A. Aleksandrov, V. M. Shabaev
arxiv-2303-16273.description: Abstract In the present study, we consider the effects of vacuum birefringence and dichroism in strong electromagnetic fields. According to quantum electrodynamics, the vacuum state exhibits different refractive properties depending on the probe photon polarization and one also obtains different probabilities of the photon decay via production of electron-positron pairs.

arxiv-2306-04525.title: Analysing the Robustness of NSGA-II under Noise
arxiv-2306-04525.creator: Duc-Cuong Dang, Andre Opris, Bahare Salehi, Dirk Sudholt
arxiv-2306-04525.description: Abstract Runtime analysis has produced many results on the efficiency of simple evolutionary algorithms like the (1+1) EA, and its analogue called GSEMO in evolutionary multiobjective optimisation (EMO). Recently, the first runtime analyses of the famous and highly cited EMO algorithm NSGA-II have emerged, demonstrating that practical algorithms with thousands of applications can be rigorously analysed.

arxiv-2412-01751.title: Estimation of the Plant Controller Communication Time-Delay Considering PMSG-Based Wind Turbines
arxiv-2412-01751.creator: Pablo Marchi † \dagger , Pablo Gill Estevez ∗ * , Alejandro Otero † ⁣ ∗ \dagger* and Cecilia Galarza † ⁣ ∗ \dagger*
arxiv-2412-01751.description: Abstract The communication control delay between the inverters and the power plant controller can be caused by several factors related to the communication link between them. Under undesirable conditions, high delay values can produce oscillations in the wind power plant that can affect the rest of the power system.

arxiv-2509-06580.title: AI for Scientific Discovery is a Social Problem
arxiv-2509-06580.creator: Georgia Channing, Avijit Ghosh
arxiv-2509-06580.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence promises to accelerate scientific discovery, yet its benefits remain unevenly distributed. While technical obstacles such as scarce data, fragmented standards, and unequal access to computation are significant, we argue that the primary barriers are social and institutional.

arxiv-2602-08300.title: “I Can’t Keep Up”: Accessibility Barriers in Video-Based Learning for Individuals with Borderline Intellectual Functioning Conference: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Fac
arxiv-2602-08300.creator: Hyehyun Chu, Seungju Kim, Chen Zhou, Yu-Kai Hung, Saelyne Yang, Hyun W. Ka, Juho Kim
arxiv-2602-08300.description: Abstract . Video-based learning (VBL) has become a dominant method for learning practical skills, yet accessibility guidelines provide limited guidance for users with cognitive differences. In particular, challenges that individuals with Borderline Intellectual Functioning (BIF) encounter in video-based learning remain largely underexplored, despite VBL’s potential to support their learning through features like self-paced viewing and visual demonstration.

arxiv-2602-11513.title: Differentially Private and Communication Efficient Large Language Model Split Inference via Stochastic Quantization and Soft Prompt
arxiv-2602-11513.creator: Yujie Gu, Richeng Jin, Xiaoyu Ji, Yier Jin, Wenyuan Xu
arxiv-2602-11513.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance and received significant research interest. The enormous computational demands, however, hinder the local deployment on devices with limited resources. The current prevalent LLM inference paradigms require users to send queries to the service providers for processing, which raises critical privacy concerns.

pmc-10623851.creator: Weiguang Gu, Wenya Zhuang, Mengxia Zhuang, Minhong He, Zhihua Li
pmc-10623851.description: BackgroundDNA damage response and repair (DDR) genes are crucial for maintaining the integrity of the genome. This study aims to explore the correlation of DDR gene mutations with TMB, clinical characteristics, and outcomes to platinum-based chemotherapy and platinum-based chemotherapy/immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without EGFR and ALK alterations.

pmc-11349981.title: Green flame-retardant rigid polyurethane foam with cobalt hydroxystannate to improve the thermal stability, flame retardancy and smoke suppression properties
pmc-11349981.creator: Xu Zhang, Zhaoqian Wang, Simiao Sun, Zhi Wang, Hua Xie
pmc-11349981.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The ecological benefits and concerns surrounding fossil fuels had led to increased interest in bio-based rigid polyurethane foam (RPUF). Nonetheless, due to its flammability, it had limited application in various fields. To solve this problem, a green bio-flame retardant, cobalt hydroxystannate (CoSn(OH)6), was prepared and compounded with montmorillonite (MMT) and chick feather protein (CF), and applied to RPUF, which not only realized the regeneration of resources, but also provided RPUF with better thermal stability, flame retardancy and smoke suppression properties.

pmc-11674292.title: Impact of Cognitive VR vs. Traditional Training on Emotional Self-Efficacy and Cognitive Function in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Retrospective Study Focusing on Gender Differences
pmc-11674292.creator: Maria Grazia Maggio, Alessandra Benenati, Federica Impellizzeri, Amelia Rizzo, Martina Barbera, Antonino Cannavò, Vera Gregoli, Giovanni Morone, Francesco Chirico, Angelo Quartarone, Rocco Salvatore Calabrò
pmc-11674292.description: Background and aim: While conventional MS rehabilitation primarily addresses physical and cognitive symptoms, recent advances in VR technology offer immersive environments that facilitate both emotional and cognitive skill development. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of VR-based training on emotional self-efficacy in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and examine its association with cognitive function improvement.

pmc-11712448.description: BackgroundAutosomal dominant Alzheimer disease (ADAD) is characterized by genetic mutations affecting the beta‐amyloid (Aß) pathway. However, vascular and immune factors play important roles which are not completely understood. Understanding the function of the neurovascular unit (NVU) comprised of neurons, glial cells, and vasculature, at different disease stages appears ideal to developing and evaluating therapeutics.

pmc-13076812.title: An immunobiliary single-cell atlas resolves crosstalk between type 2 conventional dendritic cells and γδ T cells in cholangitis
pmc-13076812.creator: Stefan Thomann, Helene Hemmer, Ankit Agrawal, Sukanya Basu, Judith Schaf, Nadine Vornberger, Tobias Krammer, Sagar, Fabian Imdahl, Tanja Poth, Marcell Tóth, Christina E. Zielinski, Tobias Poch, Jenny Krause, Andreas Rosenwald, Katja Breitkopf-Heinlein, Nuh Rahbari, Dominic Grün
pmc-13076812.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The liver biliary niche serves as a reservoir of tissue-resident immune cells and supports tissue fibrosis upon damage, yet the role of peribiliary immune cells during cholangitis remains poorly understood. Here, we induce cholestatic liver injury mirroring human biliary diseases with bile acid retention in mice to establish a spatial and multimodal single-cell RNA-sequencing atlas of the liver and liver-draining lymph nodes (LN).

pmc-13367352.title: Core Symptoms and Candidate Targets for Symptom Management in Late Pregnancy: A Network Analysis
pmc-13367352.creator: Xingruo Zhang, Yunfeng Zhao, Jiani Yang, Jing Xu, Panpan Jiang, Yanxia Zhu, Tingyu Mu, Yuhong Li
pmc-13367352.description: PurposeWomen in late pregnancy experience multiple co-occurring physical and psychological symptoms that may affect daily functioning and well-being. However, conventional approaches are limited in identifying priority intervention targets within complex symptom patterns. This study aimed to identify core symptoms and potential targets for symptom management using a network-based approach.

pmc-13413211.title: Effects of Foot Progression Angle and Stance Width on Lower-Limb Muscle Activation During the Holding Phase of Forward Lunge Exercises in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Within-Participant Crossover Study
pmc-13413211.creator: Ho-Jin Shin, Hong-Min Kim, Hwi-Young Cho, Sung-Hyeon Kim
pmc-13413211.description: Background/Objectives: This study examined whether foot progression angle and stance width modify lower-limb muscle activation during the holding phase of forward lunges in healthy adults. Methods: Thirty-six healthy adults completed five randomized within-participant lunge conditions: standard stance with 0°, 30°, and 60° foot progression angles and narrow and wide stances with a 0° foot progression angle.

pmc-13457260.title: Comparative Evaluation of Pain Perception Following Topical Application of Clove Oil, EMLA 5%, and Lignocaine Hydrochloride Gel 2% as a Pre-anesthetic Agent in Children Aged 7–10 Years: A Randomized Controlled Study
pmc-13457260.creator: Neha Awasthi, Yanina Singh, Sukhdeep Singh, Dhirja Goel, Tamanna Singla, Ashima Tyagi, Farha N Ahamed
pmc-13457260.description: Aims and objectiveThe topical anesthetic potential of clove, despite its long-standing use in dentistry, remains largely underexplored in clinical research. Hence, the present study aims to compare the pain perception following topical application of clove oil, EMLA 5%, and lignocaine hydrochloride gel 2% in 7–10-year-old children in a randomized controlled trial.

pmc-13581480.title: A twisted tale of limbs: fibular aplasia with tibial campomelia and oligosyndactyly
pmc-13581480.creator: Gahana Kataria, Vaishali Dhawan
pmc-13581480.description: on the opposite side. These findings were consistent with the fibular aplasia-tibial campomelia-oligosyndactyly (FATCO) spectrum, an uncommon congenital anomaly involving defective mesenchymal development of the lower limb.
